nicole_sales: TL;DR - SapphireBank wants Private VPC POC for LLM inference. Must preserve client L3 source IPs for IDS, require mutual TLS to connector, and want as-tight-as-possible firewall rules. Also asked whether choosing PrivateLink vs Peering affects POC cost and SLA. Need clear handoff doc and a short allowlist they can give to their firewall team.

leo_se: Short answers: mTLS supported. L3 source preservation = only with peering/transit path or an IP-preserve passthrough; PrivateLink -> connector ENI NATs source. PrivateLink is faster to stand up for locked-down VPCs.

marta_netops: If they absolutely need L3 preservation, we must do VPC peering or attach to a TGW and configure routing so the connector doesn't SNAT. That requires symmetric routing and route table updates on their side + SG changes. PrivateLink requires only outbound allowlist to our ENIs.

dan_engineering: Pricing/ops: managed static egress IPs are an add-on for Private deployments (one-time setup + monthly per-EIP + small egress surcharge). Dedicated reserved capacity can bundle static IPs cheaper per-month. Peering itself doesn't change Redwood platform price but TGW/peer data transfer might be billed by cloud provider.

nicole_sales: They said compliance won't accept X-Forwarded-For header as authoritative. They need true L3 source preserved. Can we still demo quickly?

marta_netops: Fast path for demo: provision PrivateLink with static test EIPs for firewall allowlist and hand them short-lived mTLS certs to validate connectivity and TLS. Parallel track: start peering design for L3 preservation (1-2 business days). POC can run functional tests while peering is implemented.

leo_se: Minimal allowlist (confirm final EIPs with infra):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 44.212.99.11, 44.212.99.12 (Redwood privatelink ENI samples)
- Allow outbound TCP 8443 for management to: 44.212.99.13 (optional)
- DNS UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver
- NTP UDP 123 (recommended)
- Allow return ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for NAT flows
- Allow ICMP type 3/4 for PMTU discovery

dan_engineering: MTU note: many SD-WAN appliances lower MTU; recommend testing with `ping -M do -s 1400 <peer-ip>` and enable MSS clamping if needed. If they see TLS hangs, MTU is a common cause.

marta_netops: Peering/L3-preserve checklist (high level):
- Agree non-overlapping CIDRs and route plan
- Add peering/TGW attachment and propagate routes
- Update their route tables to point to peering for connector subnets
- Update SGs to allow ingress from customer CIDR to connector ports (443,8443)
- Disable SNAT on path to connector to preserve src IP
- Test failover path and ensure return routing is correct

infra-bot: warning: infra change freeze window 2025-06-30 22:00-2025-07-01 04:00 UTC may delay ENI creation if requested within window.

leo_se: curl test snippets (we'll provide short-lived test certs):
- mTLS: `curl --cert poc-client.crt --key poc-client.key -v https://sapphire.privatelink.redwood.ai:443/healthz`
- non-mTLS: `curl -v https://sapphire.privatelink.redwood.ai:443/healthz`

Add: if using peering and L3 preserve, ensure their IDS sees the client IP from packet captures.

dan_engineering: Pricing note for sales email: include one-time setup fee for static egress, monthly per-EIP fee, per-GB egress surcharge, and discounted pricing if they buy 12mo reserved GPUs. I'll draft a short quote.

nicole_sales: Action items: 1) Marta to share test EIPs and allowlist by EOD, 2) Leo to prepare mTLS certs + curl scripts, 3) Dan to prepare pricing delta. I'll loop in sapphire-netops contact once EIPs available. Any blockers?

marta_netops: No blockers other than needing sapphire's firewall contact (name + engineering email) and awareness of infra freeze.

nicole_sales: Contact is 'harry.firewall@sapphirebank.com' - I'll intro after EIPs. Thanks team :raised_hands:
